Description: Student's net self-assessment is that the tool helped their learning. Apply when a net positive direction is stated ("positive", "helpful", "mostly positive"), even if drawbacks are also mentioned; capture drawbacks as Tier 2 drivers.
Do NOT apply when: Pros and cons are weighed with NO stated net direction (-> IM03). The stated benefit is hypothetical because they do not use AI (-> IM05).
Distinguish from: IM03 (stated net direction vs. unresolved trade-off)
Example responses: "Positive, I have received help outside of class when I could not attend office hours." • "I would say overall positive in understanding concepts but maybe negative in being able to solve the problems on my own" (net direction stated -> IM01 + Tier 2 drivers) • "Very positive, helps break problems down into steps"

Description: Student's net self-assessment is that the tool hindered their learning or was a net negative.
Do NOT apply when: A net positive or no net direction is stated (-> IM01/IM03). The student reports no impact (-> IM04).
Example responses: "I hate generative AI I think it's making me a dumber and worse students." • "Pretty bad honestly." • "Negative. I think it's better not to use it as it hinders effective learning and deep thinking."

Description: Student weighs both pros and cons with active conflict or trade-offs and does NOT state a net direction, or explicitly says the impact is both positive and negative.
Do NOT apply when: A net direction is stated despite caveats (-> IM01/IM02: code the net direction and put the caveats in Tier 2).
Distinguish from: IM01/IM02 (the deciding question: did the student state which way it nets out?)
Example responses: "Positive for understanding concepts but negative when actually solving given problems." • "It is both positive and negative on my learning." • "I think it helps teach me but it makes me less motivated to work things out myself"

Description: Student USES (or has used) AI but reports it did not move the needle or had zero net effect.
Do NOT apply when: The student states they do not or have not used AI in this course (-> IM05). Pros and cons are actively weighed (-> IM03).
Distinguish from: IM05 (no effect from use vs. no use); IM03
Example responses: "It didn't really affect my learning much. I would say my own personal effort affected my learning the most." • "Neutral. Neither helped drastically or hindered me drastically." • "It honestly hasn't made much of an impact, I haven't used AI much." (minimal use with explicit no-impact judgment)

Description: Student states they do not use, or have not used, AI tools in this course, so the impact question does not apply to them. Speculation about future or hypothetical impact does not change this code. Tier 2 codes MAY be applied when the student gives concrete reasons for non-use that match a Tier 2 code (e.g., Technical Failure).
Do NOT apply when: The student uses AI minimally but still renders an impact judgment (-> IM01-IM04 per the judgment).
Distinguish from: IM04 (no use vs. no effect from use)
Example responses: "I have not used AI tools for learning in this course specifically." • "I haven't used AI in EK 301" • "I didn't use AI" • "Haven't used AI in this course" • "Not applicable yet."

Description: Responses that provide no codable data: 'N/A', blank, nonsensical, or failing to address the prompt. Standalone; select no Tier 2 codes.
Do NOT apply when: Any other Tier 1 code can be applied, even at low confidence (apply it and flag instead). Note: a bare "N/A" defaults here, but "N/A, I don't use AI" is IM05.

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Use of AI to break down concepts, explain the 'bigger picture', or clarify confusing lecture topics.
Do NOT apply when: The described use is checking work or finding mistakes (-> IM08).
Example responses: "they help explain the concepts and steps for solving problems" • "it can answer my very specific question, and in context" • "It helped me understand more"

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Use of AI as a diagnostic tool to check intermediate steps, check answers, find mistakes, or confirm methodology.
Do NOT apply when: The described use is explaining concepts (-> IM07).
Example responses: "It's helped me learn and check my answers" • "they make it easy to verify my work and see where I may have gone wrong" • "makes checking for mistakes easier without having to wait for the posted answers"

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Valuation of AI for its efficiency, speed, or availability outside standard office hours. Includes dialogic availability: the ability to ask unlimited or immediate follow-up questions.
Do NOT apply when: Speed/availability is not mentioned as part of the value.
Distinguish from: IM07/IM08 (WHY it helps: availability vs. content)
Example responses: "almost always available and flexible to use versus office hours" • "I have received help outside of class when I could not attend office hours" • "much more accessible and less time consuming then having to go to oh or discussion" • "I like that I can always ask follow up questions."

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Hindrance to the student's own cognitive process: reports of feeling 'lazy', over-reliant, losing critical thinking or problem-solving skill, or fear thereof from their own use.
Do NOT apply when: The student only states the tool is good IF used correctly, without reporting actual or feared harm to their own cognition (-> IM13). Both can co-occur.
Example responses: "1 think I've gotten lazier with solving problems" • "the negative effect is that i rely on it too much" • "it also limits my thinking abilities" • "perhaps negative for times I feel like not engaging with the AI and allowing it to answer questions, weakening my problem solving skills"

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Failure of the AI to perform the academic task correctly: wrong math, hallucination, inability to interpret mechanics diagrams or images.
Do NOT apply when: The AI's content is accurate but its teaching approach or presentation is unhelpful (-> IM12).
Example responses: "sometimes can confuse you by giving wrong answers" • "the AI tools so far have lack of ability to correctly analyze the images of mechanics problems" • "While AI isn't always correct about the final answer"

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Frustration with the AI's teaching methods, explanation structure, or clarity, regardless of technical accuracy: strange strategies, misalignment with course material, vague or nonspecific explanations.
Do NOT apply when: The complaint is that the AI's content is factually or mathematically wrong (-> IM11).
Example responses: "it can teach strange strategies or systems of solving that don't align with how th[e course teaches]" • "tips for solving mechanics problems based on online resources, which are mixed and nonspecific"

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Recognition that the tool's impact is tied to user behavior: AI is only positive 'if used correctly' and negative if misused.
Do NOT apply when: The student reports actual or feared harm to their own cognition without conditional framing (-> IM10 alone).
Example responses: "If applied correctly it is a useful tool, but it can easily be extremely negative for learning if not used properly" • "I think its positive if used correctly" • "There are ways to use tools that can negatively impact learning, while there are also ways to positively enhance learning."

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: Emotional or confidence-related benefit: reduced frustration or stress, increased confidence, comfort asking questions without judgment, feeling supported or less stuck.
Do NOT apply when: The benefit described is purely functional (content explained -> IM07; work checked -> IM08; speed/availability -> IM09) with no emotional or confidence dimension stated.
Distinguish from: IM09 (convenience vs. emotional relief); IM07; IM14
Example responses: "Very positive, eased the frustration gap while also allowing me to learn with assistance."

Tier: Tier 2: Drivers of Sentiment (select all that apply)
Description: A specific driver of sentiment is stated but fits no other Tier 2 code, even partially. Apply this code AND describe the novel driver in the notes field. A generic restatement of positivity or helpfulness is NOT a driver; check IM07-IM13 and IM15 first, and prefer a partial fit over this residual.
Do NOT apply when: Any other Tier 2 code fits, even partially or at low confidence (apply it and flag instead). The driver is emotional or confidence-related (-> IM15). No specific driver is stated (leave Tier 2 empty; an empty Tier 2 is valid).
Example responses: "I'll be so doomed if there's no AI because [of language related difficulties], it's hard for me to read and understand by using textbooks" (language accessibility driver)
